cross_market_insights: Search demand is small in Australia (10/month for the head term and every 'foreigner' variant; 30 for 'wedding in france') and larger in the UK (110 head term, 260 'wedding in france'). This page earns its place as a trust and AI Overview/PAA citation asset and the legal companion to /destinations/europe/france, not as a traffic play.

Only one Australia-specific result anywhere (a Paris celebrant page, Sydney #5). Melbourne's #1 is the Australian Embassy's short page; nobody explains the route from Australia end to end: residency reality, DFAT documents, apostilles, translations, symbolic ceremony, and recognition at home.
Residency figures conflict across ranking pages and the AI Overview (30 days, 40 days, 'not required', 'one month'). An officially sourced, clear answer is the main gap.

Related searches ask 'from australia', 'for foreigners', 'how to register marriage in France' and 'types of marriage in France'; PAA asks 'Can foreigners legally get married in France?' and 'How much does it cost to get married in France?'.
Brisbane and London top 3 are weak (traditions pages, French-learning blog, old forums), so a well-sourced 2026 guide has a realistic path to page one.
UK pages and the AI Overview already push the two-step route (legal at home, ceremony in France); for Australians that means the Australian NOIM and celebrant route, which no ranking page explains.
payload.recommended_angle: Answer the title honestly in the first screen: a legal marriage in France needs a residence link (per the run-log decision, official sources say at least one partner must be a French citizen or legally resident with a period of residence in the commune), so most Australian couples marry legally at home and hold the celebration in France. Then give both routes properly: the legal route for those who qualify (documents from Australia, apostilles, sworn translations, banns, the mairie) and the symbolic route done well (Australian legal ceremony first, then the French wedding week), with recognition at home sourced to Australian government pages.
